english.title: Trespass with intent to search for or to pursue hares with dogs
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF THE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 63 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
trespassed on land with the intention of
using OR
facilitating / encouraging the use of OR
enabling another person to observe the use of
a dog
to search for / pursue a hare

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 63(2) provides a defence of reasonable excuse.
(ii) Section 64 makes it an offence to have an article with intention that it will be used in the course of or in connection with the commission of this offence, see H100779.
(iii) Section 65 provides for recovery orders on conviction of an offence under this section.
(iv) Where a dog was used in or was present at the commission of this offence, see section 66 for disqualification orders.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 51 weeks imprisonment and / or a fine.

In relation to an offence committed before section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes into force, the reference to 51 weeks imprisonment is to be read as a reference to 6 months.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
